summary.goal: Redis/BullMQ integration for reliable task scheduling with concurrency limits, priority handling, and fair distribution across runs.

acceptance_criteria.description: BullMQ queue 'forge:tasks' with configurable concurrency limit
Priority field on jobs - higher priority tasks processed first
Fair scheduling across runs via round-robin or weighted distribution
Automatic retry on transient failures (configurable attempts)
Dead letter queue 'forge:tasks:failed' for permanently failed tasks
Job events trigger Forgemaster state updates
Worker processor triggers agent spawn via AgentSpawner callback
Redis connection failure throws explicit error with message: 'Redis is required for task scheduling. Ensure Redis is running at {REDIS_URL}'

observations: BullMQ is battle-tested for job queues in Node.js
Redis provides persistence and pub/sub for real-time updates
Fair scheduling prevents one large run from starving others
Worker processor is the integration point with forge-relay-integration
patterns: Job data contains task_id, run_id - lookup from DB for full context
Worker processes dequeue and trigger agent spawn via callback
concerns: Redis is a REQUIRED dependency - Forgemaster must fail fast on startup if Redis is unavailable with clear error message. NO silent fallback to in-memory queue in production.

architect.redis_requirement: REQUIRED - no fallback in production. InMemoryTaskQueue only for automated tests.

steps.title: Create TaskQueue interface
steps.description: Define interface for task queue operations abstracting Redis/BullMQ details

acceptance_criteria.description: TaskQueue interface: enqueue(taskId, runId, priority), getQueueStats()
JobHandle type: { jobId, taskId, runId, priority, attempts }
QueueStats type: { pending, active, completed, failed, delayed }
onTaskReady callback type: (job: JobHandle) => Promise<void>

specification.pattern_description: Use same interface-first pattern for dependency injection

steps.title: Implement BullMQ task queue
steps.description: Implement TaskQueue using BullMQ with Redis backend

acceptance_criteria.description: BullMQTaskQueue class implements TaskQueue interface
Constructor takes Redis connection options and queue name ('forge:tasks')
Priority field on jobs (higher = processed first)
Configurable retry attempts (default 3) with exponential backoff
Dead letter queue 'forge:tasks:failed' for permanent failures
Connection failure throws RedisConnectionError with actionable message: 'Failed to connect to Redis at {url}. Ensure Redis is running.'

architecture.error_handling: Throw RedisConnectionError on connection failure - do NOT fall back to in-memory

steps.title: Create queue worker processor
steps.description: BullMQ Worker that dequeues tasks and triggers agent spawn via callback

acceptance_criteria.description: createQueueWorker(queue, onTaskReady) factory function
Configurable concurrency (default 5 parallel tasks)
onTaskReady callback receives JobHandle, must return Promise<void>
Worker events for 'completed', 'failed', 'error' logging
onTaskReady callback is the integration point - caller provides agent spawn logic

architecture.integration: onTaskReady callback provided by forge-relay-integration for agent spawning

steps.title: Implement fair scheduling across runs
steps.description: Prevent single large run from starving others via fair distribution

acceptance_criteria.description: TaskScheduler class manages task enqueueing with fairness
Round-robin selection when multiple runs have ready tasks
Per-run concurrency limits (configurable, default 2 tasks per run)
scheduleReadyTasks(runId) finds and enqueues all ready tasks for a run
Respects run.has_pending_gate flag - skips scheduling if gate pending

steps.title: Create in-memory queue for tests only
steps.description: In-memory queue implementation ONLY for automated tests - NOT for production or development use

acceptance_criteria.description: InMemoryTaskQueue implements TaskQueue interface
Priority queue using sorted array or heap
Clearly documented as TEST-ONLY with JSDoc @internal tag
Constructor logs warning: 'InMemoryTaskQueue is for tests only. Use BullMQ in production.'
File path: src/queue/__tests__/InMemoryTaskQueue.ts (in test directory)

specification.purpose: TEST-ONLY implementation for unit/integration tests without Redis dependency
specification.location: Place in __tests__ directory to make test-only nature clear
specification.warning: Constructor emits console.warn if NODE_ENV is not 'test'

steps.title: Create task queue factory with explicit Redis requirement
steps.description: Factory function that creates BullMQ queue with clear Redis requirement

acceptance_criteria.description: createTaskQueue(config) returns BullMQTaskQueue - no fallback option
Config: { redisUrl: string (REQUIRED), queueName?: string, concurrency?: number }
Throws ConfigurationError if redisUrl not provided: 'REDIS_URL environment variable is required'
Validates Redis connection at startup, throws if unavailable
NO FORGE_QUEUE_TYPE env var - Redis is always required in production

architecture.no_fallback: No in-memory fallback. Redis is required. Fail fast with clear error.

steps.title: Connect queue worker to Forgemaster orchestration
steps.description: Wire up the queue worker's onTaskReady callback to trigger agent spawning

acceptance_criteria.description: ForgemasterService class orchestrates queue, storage, and spawner
onTaskReady callback: load task from storage, prepare workspace, spawn agent
Task status updated to 'running' when dequeued
If task has gate (step.gate defined), create Gate instead of spawning agent

architecture.pattern: Orchestration service composing queue, storage, and spawner
architecture.gate_detection: Check forgeStep.gate before spawning - route to gate handling if present
